title: Coffee reflexes — slow-motion camera orbit test

assistant_visual_review.method: 25 sampled frames over 0–10s, 13 drop/transition samples, 9 catch-contact samples and full decoded-frame inspection.
observations: Forward FPP running follows the cafe sidewalk; the patron exits the far left early.
A left-facing view at about 1.6s reveals a mug already separated from the empty hand.
TPP begins around 2.6s. From about 2.9–7.5s the camera makes a broad circular move around Riley, with changing cafe/rail background perspective.
Finger-to-mug contact is visible around 3.5–3.75s; the orbit continues while she holds the cup.
Handback is visible around 7.9–8.8s, followed by Riley running away. Gold outfit, skin/chrome styling and cyberpunk setting broadly follow references.
limitations: Patron briefly holds the cup at the extreme left in the opening frame, contrary to the requested absence before the glance.
Left-facing view and FPP-to-TPP transition read as generated angle cuts rather than a continuous head turn and camera pull-out.
The cup is airborne at the reveal but rises/floats toward camera before descending again. Gravity and scale remain imperfect.
Catch occurs around waist height instead of just above the paving.
Strongest orbit continues after contact and spends substantial time on the held cup. No precise angle or full 360-degree claim.
Likeness and hand contact need playback scrutiny. Exit reads as a run with a cyan trail; super-speed acceleration still needs polish.
Native audio was extracted and level-checked only; no independent listening, speech-absence verification or final mix approval.
assistant_visual_review.assistant_verdict: Circular camera motion and visible catch present; cup trajectory, rescue height and perspective transition still need polish.

user_feedback.summary: Rejected: Riley passes the man before noticing; cup rises from below and is too far away. Correct starting reference with man farther ahead. As she draws level, side glance sees cup already falling nearby, then slow-motion circular camera move.
